title: The idea that refused to stay on paper

story.about: The gap between the world you imagine and the material you have to make it. A small paper boat escapes a blank page and survives an ocean; the final reveal shows this world was made from a brief and edited in AutoPromote.
story.whyCare: Everyone has an idea they cannot yet turn into something others can see. The fragile boat makes that struggle visible.
story.hook: A paper boat on a desk moves as the desk becomes an ocean. Impossible but immediately readable.
story.beginning: A single ordinary sheet becomes a boat; one idea, no footage.
story.development: The boat becomes the central subject of a much larger cinematic world.
story.tension: A dark wave threatens the fragile boat. Will the idea survive becoming real?
story.payoff: A warm path of light opens across the ocean; the boat survives. The camera reveals the created world as editable material in the real AutoPromote Studio.
story.ending: The finished world fills the screen again: A brief. No footage. AutoPromote.
story.withheld: The origin of the footage and the AutoPromote identity until the payoff.

assets.prompt: Photoreal cinematic miniature world, tactile ivory origami paper boat with one crisp triangular sail and sharply folded hull, no writing on the paper. Warm amber practical light against deep petrol-blue shadows, natural film contrast, 35mm commercial cinematography. The same single small ivory paper boat is the only hero object. Extreme close-up at table level. A small ivory origami sailboat rests on a dark wooden desk beside one blank sheet of paper. A thin shimmering pool of water slowly spreads underneath the boat; the boat lifts gently and floats as the desk surface becomes a deep blue ocean. An impossible transformation shown with physically convincing water and crisp stable folds. Slow controlled camera push. Quiet amber light from the left. One uninterrupted five-second shot.
